note: The days that shape what gets cooked. Used to filter the collection and to surface the right recipes as each one comes around.

occasions.name: No time tonight
occasions.blurb: Fifteen minutes or less, mostly from the cupboard.

occasions.name: Thanksgiving
occasions.blurb: A centerpiece worth gathering around, and the sides that carry the table.

occasions.name: Winter holidays
occasions.blurb: Christmas, Hanukkah, a long dark week of people in the house.

occasions.name: New Year
occasions.blurb: Black-eyed peas for luck, and something bright after a fortnight of rich food.

occasions.name: Spring table
occasions.blurb: Easter, Passover, the first warm Sunday — green, light and pretty.

occasions.name: Cookout
occasions.blurb: Grill food that isn't an afterthought for the people not eating burgers.

occasions.name: Labor Day
occasions.blurb: The last big cookout of the summer, when the garden is at full tilt.

occasions.name: Picnic
occasions.blurb: Travels in a cooler, survives three hours on a table, no mayonnaise anxiety.

occasions.name: Potluck
occasions.blurb: Feeds a crowd, travels in the dish you baked it in, good at room temperature.

occasions.name: Game day
occasions.blurb: Food people eat standing up, over a long afternoon.

occasions.name: Bake sale
occasions.blurb: Travels well, slices cleanly, sells out first.

occasions.name: Brunch
occasions.blurb: Assembled the night before so the morning is calm.

occasions.name: Feeding someone else
occasions.blurb: New baby, illness, a hard week — food that arrives ready to reheat and freeze.

occasions.name: Celebration
occasions.blurb: The nights worth cooking something ambitious.
